evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/state.rs:855 declares `pub sso_sessions: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, PendingSsoSession>>>` (initialized empty at state.rs:1010). This map holds the per-login OAuth CSRF `state` id plus the PKCE `code_verifier` for the web SSO flow between `/api/v1/sso/login` and `/api/v1/sso/callback`.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:275-285 (sso_callback): the callback does `state.sso_sessions.lock().await.remove(&session_id).ok_or_else(|| invalid_state)`. Because the pending session lives only in this process's memory, ANY deployment with more than one reality-server replica behind a load balancer will route `/sso/login` and `/sso/callback` to different instances on a fraction of logins -> the callback's `remove` misses -> every such login fails with HTTP 400 `invalid_state`. A rolling deploy / restart between login and callback drops ALL in-flight logins the same way. reality-server is the PUBLIC multi-region portal (REGION sk/cz/eu per backend/servers/CLAUDE.md), i.e. exactly the deployment shape where >1 replica is expected.

This is an UNACKNOWLEDGED instance of a constraint the codebase already documents elsewhere: state.rs:406-410 explicitly notes the mobile SSO token store is an in-process `Mutex<HashMap>`, is 'not durable', and that a Redis-backed store is a tracked follow-up because 'reality-server has no Redis'. The web-PKCE `sso_sessions` map at state.rs:855 shares that single-instance limitation but carries NO such comment, and its failure mode is worse than durability loss: it is user-facing login breakage under horizontal scale, not just a cold-start reset.

Reachability: unauthenticated public web SSO login path; triggered by normal operation as soon as reality-server runs >1 replica or is restarted mid-login. No attacker required. Severity bounded to availability of the login flow (no data exposure, no auth bypass) -> MEDIUM.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the in-memory type, the empty init, and the remove-or-invalid_state branch are confirmed by direct read; the production replica count / LB affinity config was not inspected on this cloud runner, so whether it bites today depends on deployment topology.

Fix direction: back the pending-session map with the same durable/shared store the mobile-token follow-up (state.rs:406-410) calls for (Redis or DB with the existing PENDING_SSO_SESSION_TTL_MINUTES=10 TTL, sso.rs:26), or enforce sticky sessions at the LB as an interim mitigation and add a comment at state.rs:855 documenting the constraint. Likely shares the infra follow-up blocking the mobile-token store.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs returns raw internal error strings to the client in the SsoError `error_description` field at 10 sites: sso_callback (303 token_exchange_failed, 313 user_info_failed, 325 user_create_failed, 337 session_create_failed), create_mobile_sso_token (460 invalid_token, 477 user_info_failed, 489 token_create_failed), validate_mobile_sso_token (541 invalid_token, 553 user_create_failed, 565 session_create_failed). Each passes `&e.to_string()` straight into `SsoError::new(code, &e.to_string())`, which is serialized as JSON back to the HTTP caller.

For `user_create_failed` (325, 553) and `session_create_failed` (337, 565) the `e` is the underlying anyhow/sqlx error, so a DB-layer error message (constraint names, column/table hints, connection detail) can be reflected verbatim to an unauthenticated public caller. For `token_exchange_failed` (303) and `user_info_failed` (313, 477) the `e` is the upstream PM-OAuth HTTP error, which can reveal internal PM OAuth hostnames / endpoint paths / status text.

Contrast with the adjacent correct pattern in the SAME file: sso.rs:368-378 (build_portal_session_cookie failure) logs the detail server-side via `tracing::error!(error = e, ...)` and returns a GENERIC 'Failed to build session cookie' to the client. listings.rs:739-744 / 780-785 do the same ('Internal server error' to client, `tracing::error!(error = %e, ...)` server-side). The SSO error branches skip that redaction and leak `e` directly.

Reachability: sso_callback is reachable unauthenticated (it is the public OAuth redirect target); the mobile token endpoints are reachable by anyone who can POST. Info-disclosure only (no RCE / no direct auth bypass) -> MEDIUM.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the `&e.to_string()` arguments and the JSON SsoError serialization are confirmed by direct read; the exact sensitivity of each leaked string depends on the upstream/DB error text, which was not runtime-captured.

Fix (cloud-landable, backend-only): mirror the existing redaction pattern -- `tracing::error!(error = %e, "<context>")` server-side and return a stable generic `error_description` per code (e.g. 'Authentication failed', 'Could not complete sign-in'), at all 10 sites. One-to-two line change per branch, no new deps.
